title: What is LGS1920 Studio?
description: A plain-language introduction to LGS1920 Studio, its workflow, its exports, and what you need to get started.

hero.title: What is Studio, and what can you do with it?
hero.lead: Studio is a privacy-first browser application for turning an outdoor route into a map presentation and a video you can share on social network, enriched with dynamic points of interest, cinematic camera angles, and synchronized multimedia data to create an immersive narrative of your outdoor adventures.

sectionNav.label: What it creates
sectionNav.summary: Video for social networks, snapshots, and reports

overview.title: A workspace for an outdoor route you already have.
intro: Studio is a web application that opens directly in a browser. You load an existing route file, view it on a 2D or 3D map, and prepare a clear presentation of the journey.

You can adjust the route, add points of interest and useful information, choose what the camera shows, and prepare a replay for a shareable video. Snapshots and reports remain available when you prefer a still or documentary format. Studio is used after or around an outing; it does not record the activity while you are outdoors.
overview.simpleIntro: Default settings allow you to start and create your first video very easily, but you have access to many other settings to go much further.

basics.title: Start with a route file
basics.body: Load a GeoJSON, GPX, or KML file created by a GPS device, a mobile application, another mapping tool, or one of the Studio samples.

basics.title: Explore a global, 3D playground in the browser!
basics.body: Inspect the route on the map, change its appearance, add context, and prepare the view without installing a traditional desktop editor.

basics.title: Prepare and share a video
basics.body: Prepare a replay, record a video, and export it for Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, or another social network. Snapshots and PDF or HTML reports remain available when you need them.

items.title: Privacy first
items.body: Your data stays with you: browser, device, or cloud.
items.note: Cloud access will be available in a future version.

items.title: Studio is free
items.body: Studio is completely free and will remain so.
items.note: Some external services accessible through Studio may be paid services from their providers. Studio has no affiliation with any of the providers concerned.

workflow.title: A session in four steps.
workflow.intro: You do not need to know every tool before starting. A first session can follow this simple order.

steps.title: Open or import a route
steps.body: Choose a sample or load a GeoJSON, GPX, or KML file from your device.

steps.title: Check the journey
steps.body: Make sure the route, tracks, and points of interest appear in the right place.

steps.title: Prepare the presentation
steps.body: Choose the map, colors, camera view, replay, and any text or statistics you want to show.

steps.title: Record and share
steps.body: Replay the journey, record the video, then export it on social network or download it.

outputs.title: The main result: a video you can share.
outputs.intro: The video workflow is the main way to present a journey. Snapshots and reports remain available as alternatives when a still image or document is more useful.

items.title: Video for social networks
items.body: Replay the journey and record the map scene, camera movement, and visible widgets. Export the result for Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, or another social network.

items.title: Snapshots
items.body: Create a still image of the current map, route, camera view, and visible information.

items.title: Reports
items.body: Generate a PDF document or a packaged HTML report with route information, statistics, points of interest, and maps.

practical.title: A few useful things to know.
practical.intro: Studio is designed to be opened and tried directly. These points explain the main technical requirements without requiring specialist knowledge.

items.title: Your working data stays local by default
items.body: Route files and the current project are handled in the browser unless you explicitly use a synchronization or external service.

items.title: Use a recent browser
items.body: The map needs WebGL. Video work can use more memory, so closing unused tabs may make recording smoother.

items.title: Cesium engine and free access
items.body: Studio uses Cesium, an open-source 3D globe engine, for its 2D and 3D scenes. During the trial, Studio provides shared Cesium access that may have some limitations. After the trial, a free Cesium Ion account and token are needed for Cesium-backed data and provide access to additional basemaps and 3D layers.

items.title: Optional paid providers
items.body: Studio can also give you access to paid map or data providers. These services are optional and billed by their own providers; LGS1920 has no commercial relationship with them.

basic.title: What is LGS1920 Studio?
basic.intro: Studio helps you turn an existing outdoor route into a replay and a video to share on Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, or another social network. You can also create a snapshot or report when that is more useful.

pageCta.title: Create a video and share your journey.
pageCta.body: Open Studio with a route file and prepare a video for your social networks, or use the quick guide for a short tour of the workspace.
